newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi in third trial over Fininvest affairs.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi in third trial over Fininvest affairs.

text.p: An examining magistrate on Friday sent former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi to trial for alleged false accounting related to his Fininvest group, making this the third trial faced by the media magnate.

Berlusconi, who governed Italy for seven turbulent months in 1994, is already standing trial here on charges of bribing tax inspectors in return for lenient audits of his companies and, in a separate case, for illegally channelling funds to politicians.
Milan judge Cristina Mannocci set October 20 as the opening date for the latest judicial hearing.

Prosecuting magistrate Margherita Taddei had requested trial for the businessman-turned-politician and four of his close business associates Adriano Galliani, Giancarlo Foscale, Livio Gironi and Carlo Bernasconi.
They are accused of having established an illegal slush fund when Berlusconi's media group Fininvest bought the Medusa film business in 1988.

The price for Medusa was around 30 billion lire and Berlusconi and the others are alleged in reality to have paid about 20 billion for Medusa with the remaining 10 billion alleged to have been used to establish a slush fund.
In a statement later, Fininvest reiterated the "absolute regularity" of the Medusa operation.

"The acquisition of Medusa was put into the accounts regularly and the price corresponded to the value of the company as shown by evaluations made by experts both at the moment of purchase in December 1988 and subsequently," it said.
Fininvest said full respect of rules governing accounting practices meant it could rule out not only the prosecution's allegations but also the existence of hidden funds.

Berlusconi, who still leads Italy's centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance, is already on trial for corruption along with disgraced former Socialist prime minister Bettino Craxi, himself in self-imposed exile in Tunisia.

Another trial on charges of bribing tax officials restarted from scratch earlier in February after the previous year-long proceeding was declared null and void following the resignation of its presiding judge.
